row1.revenue: Amazon leads revenue with $716.9B, outpacing Walmart by $3.7B and UnitedHealth by $269.3B, highlighting a significant gap at the top of the list. Apple and Alphabet trail further, with revenues of $416.2B and $402.8B respectively.
row1.net_income: Microsoft leads with a net income of $133.7B, outpacing Alphabet by $1.5B and NVIDIA by $13.6B, showing a clear top‑tier advantage in profitability. The gap between the top two firms is modest compared to the $56.6B difference between Microsoft and Amazon.
row1.total_assets: JPMorgan Chase leads Total Assets with 4.4 T USD, far ahead of Bank of America’s 3.4 T USD-a 1.0 T USD gap that dwarfs the 818 B USD of Amazon and the 758 B USD of Microsoft. The top two banks together hold more than 7 T USD in assets, eclipsing the tech giants by over 3 T USD.
row1.total_equity: Microsoft leads Total Equity with $442.4 B, outpacing Alphabet by $27.1 B and Amazon by $31.3 B, creating a clear 6‑to‑7 % advantage over the next tier. JPMorgan Chase and Bank of America trail further, with $362.4 B and $303.2 B respectively.
row1.total_liabilities: JPMorgan Chase (JPM) tops the list with $4.1 trillion in total liabilities, far outpacing the next‑in‑line Bank of America (BAC) at $3.1 trillion - a $1.0 trillion gap that dwarfs the $407 billion liabilities of Amazon (AMZN).
row1.cash_and_equivalents: JPMorgan Chase leads cash and equivalents with $343.3 B, outpacing Bank of America’s $239.3 B by $104 B and Amazon’s $86.8 B by $256.5 B. The gap between the top two is the largest, highlighting JPM’s dominant liquidity position.
row1.gross_profit: Amazon leads gross profit with $360.5B, outpacing Alphabet by $120.2B and Microsoft by $135.0B, highlighting a substantial gap between the top and the next tier of tech giants. The gap between Amazon and the rest of the group underscores its dominant profitability in the current fiscal year.
row1.operating_income_ebit: Microsoft leads with $155.2B operating income, outpacing Apple by $22.1B and NVIDIA by $24.8B, showing a clear top‑tier gap in EBIT.

row2_sector.revenue: Technology leads the revenue mix with $987.7B (22.0%) followed closely by Consumer Cyclical at $976.4B (21.7%), indicating a highly concentrated top‑tier dominated by tech and consumer discretionary players. The combined top two sectors account for 43.7% of total revenue, underscoring the limited diversification across the index.
row2_sector.total_assets: Financial Services dominate the portfolio with 8.1T USD, representing 63.4% of total assets, far outpacing the next largest sector, Technology, at 1.4T USD (10.6%). The remaining sectors collectively hold only about 26.6% of assets, indicating a highly concentrated exposure.
row2_sector.net_income: Technology dominates the portfolio, generating $373.0B in net income - 41.3% of total - more than double the next largest sector, Communication Services, which contributed $216.0B (23.9%). The remaining sectors collectively account for just 35.4% of net income.

row2_bubble: NVDA’s 55.6% net margin on $215.9 B revenue shows it is far more profitable than UNH, whose 2.7% margin on comparable revenue indicates lower efficiency. The stark gap highlights NVDA’s superior cost control and high-margin business model.
row3_heatmap: MA delivers the highest return on equity at 193.5%, far outpacing peers, while JPM carries the greatest leverage with a debt‑to‑equity ratio of 11.21x, indicating a higher risk profile. Companies with high ROE and low leverage, such as MA, present the most attractive risk‑adjusted performance.
row4_market_trends: GOOGL leads the group with a 66.9% 12‑month return, the highest among the highest‑revenue companies. NFLX lags far behind, posting a 32.5% decline. The spread between the top and bottom performers underscores the volatility in the sector.
